name: CGRateS
what_it_is: CGRateS is a real-time Online/Offline Charging System (OCS) for Telecom and ISP environments, implemented in Go. It provides rating, session charging, CDR processing, fraud detection, and LCR (Least Cost Routing) as independent micro-services accessible via a rich RPC API.
components: ERS (Event Reader Service — ingest from Kafka, AMQP, NATS, file, HTTP)
EES (Event Exporter Service — export CDRs/events to various targets)
Agents: DiameterAgent, RADIUSAgent, AsteriskAgent, HTTPAgent, DNSAgent, SIPAgent
measurement: StatS: real-time metrics queues (ASR, ACD, TCD, ACC, TCC, PDD, DDC, custom)
ThresholdS: event-driven threshold breach detection with configurable actions
CDR logging: full CDR storage with interim records support
Caps stats: concurrent request monitoring with configurable sampling interval
Performance target: 5000+ requests/sec on a single machine
configuration: data_db: runtime data store — *redis (default, port 6379) or *mongo
stor_db: tariff plan and CDR store — *mysql (default, port 3306), *postgres, *mongo, *internal
Tariff plans loaded from CSV files via cgr-loader or LoaderS service
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection framework; testing relies on integration test suite (integration_test.sh)
DiameterAgent and RADIUSAgent can be tested with external traffic generators
poster_attempts and failed_posts_dir provide retry/dead-letter handling for export failures
Caps strategy (*busy or *queue) can simulate overload scenarios by capping concurrent requests
modes: Online charging (prepaid/pseudoprepaid): real-time session reservation and debit
Clustered/dispatcher mode: DispatcherS routes requests across multiple cgr-engine nodes
Standalone mode: all services in a single cgr-engine process
Admin mode: cgradmin sample config enables administrative API access
constraints: data_db (Redis or MongoDB) MUST be running before cgr-engine starts; no built-in data_db
stor_db (MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL, or MongoDB) required for tariff plans and CDR persistence
Tariff plans must be pre-loaded via cgr-loader or LoaderS before rating can function
DiameterAgent requires external Diameter peer; RADIUSAgent requires RADIUS client — neither is self-contained
Session charging requires an upstream VoIP platform (e.g., FreeSWITCH, Asterisk, Kamailio) to drive session events
No docker-compose file in the repository; the devel Docker image bundles Redis, MySQL, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, and FreeSWITCH in a single container
docker_services: cgrates/cgrates (single devel image): bundles cgr-engine, Redis, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, FreeSWITCH
Integration test image (data/docker/integration): adds RabbitMQ, Kafka 3.5, NATS 2.9, MongoDB 7.0, MariaDB, PostgreSQL
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml or docker-compose.yaml file in the repository
No built-in web UI or dashboard; API-only interface
No native Kafka or NATS broker bundled in the devel image (only in integration test image)
No built-in billing invoice generation; CDR export is raw data only
No Kubernetes manifests or Helm charts provided
